actors.name: Policy Analyst (End User)
actors.description: Human researcher/decision-maker who poses a policy question and inspects the full reasoning trail.
actors.interactions: Creates simulations, configures scenario constraints, starts/pauses runs, streams progress, reads decision brief.

actors.name: Stakeholder Agent
actors.description: Autonomous institutional representative (social insurance, ministry, chamber, patient rep, etc.) with own interests, budget constraints, priorities and historical positions.
actors.interactions: Forms positions, submits arguments, responds to counterarguments, requests evidence, revises positions, forms coalitions.

actors.name: Moderator Agent
actors.description: Neutral process steward with no position of its own; translates question into a mandate, selects actors, sets rules, detects contradictions, ends negotiation.
actors.interactions: Opens/closes rounds, calls for justification, records consensus/conflict, decides stopping conditions.

actors.name: Evidence Curator / Ingestion Operator
actors.description: Backend role (human or automated) responsible for corpus ingestion quality and source authority classification.
actors.interactions: Triggers ingestion, reviews extraction quality, tunes retrieval, curates authoritative reference data.

actors.name: LLM Provider
actors.description: External probabilistic reasoning provider used by agents and moderator.
actors.interactions: Receives prompts with evidence bundles, returns structured argument/position proposals; never authoritative.

actors.name: Scheduler / Background Worker
actors.description: Executes long-running ingestion and simulation jobs asynchronously.
actors.interactions: Consumes queued jobs, emits progress events, retries on failure.

assumptions.assumption: The ~3GB 2020 press corpus is German-language, PDF/HTML mixed, with usable publication metadata.
assumptions.impactIfWrong: Extraction and provenance model must change; citation quality drops.
assumptions.mitigation: Profile corpus first; build adapter per source format; degrade gracefully to document-level provenance.

assumptions.assumption: Press reports reliably reveal institutional positions but are not ground truth on facts.
assumptions.mitigation: Model source authority tiering; require authoritative sources for quantitative claims.

assumptions.assumption: Hackathon scope: one policy question per simulation, deterministic negotiation rules, LLM for content only.
assumptions.mitigation: Freeze MVP scope; design extension points explicitly.

assumptions.assumption: LLM outputs are nondeterministic, so reproducibility is bounded by recorded prompt/model/seed metadata.
assumptions.impactIfWrong: Claims of deterministic outcomes would be false.
assumptions.mitigation: Persist full event log + prompt/model versions; document reproducibility limits.

assumptions.assumption: PostgreSQL + Qdrant are sufficient; no message broker beyond a single worker queue is needed.
assumptions.impactIfWrong: Scaling issues on large corpus ingestion.
assumptions.mitigation: Keep ingestion idempotent and parallelizable by document.

boundedContexts.name: EvidenceCorpus
boundedContexts.description: Owns the authoritative document corpus: ingestion, extraction, article segmentation, passage chunking and citation-grade provenance. Publishes passages as an open host for retrieval.
boundedContexts.subdomainRationale: Traceable evidence is the differentiator that makes the simulation credible rather than a chatbot.

invariants.rule: A Passage can never exist without a resolvable parent Article and Document with a source URI.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Orphan citation that cannot be traced to a physical page.

invariants.rule: A Document's authority tier and extraction quality are assigned at ingestion and immutable thereafter.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Retroactive authority inflation of weak sources.

invariants.rule: Passage offsets must lie within the parent Article text bounds and must not overlap sibling passages.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: A citation pointing at the wrong sentence.

invariants.rule: A Document below the extraction quality threshold cannot produce citable Passages.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Citing garbled OCR output as evidence.

invariants.rule: A QuotationBlock attributed to a natural person must never enter an EvidencePack; a quotation attributed to an institution is retained as an attributed institutional statement and stays citable with its attribution.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Quoting real persons, or losing legitimate institutional statements to an over-broad filter.

invariants.rule: Authority is evaluated per claim type: legislation outranks all for legal questions, official statistics for quantitative ones, studies for causal ones. No single universal ranking may be applied.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: A press statement outranking a statute because it scored higher on one global scale.

invariants.rule: A Document must record its source type explicitly enough to be placed in a claim-type-specific authority rule; unknown source types cannot be promoted to authoritative.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Unclassified material quietly becoming authoritative.

boundedContexts.name: EvidenceRetrieval
boundedContexts.description: Turns a claim into a balanced, scored, inspectable evidence pack. Owns hybrid search, reranking, stance classification and recency weighting. Never owns the corpus itself.
boundedContexts.subdomainRationale: Balanced supporting/contradicting evidence retrieval prevents one-sided argumentation.

invariants.rule: An EvidencePack must record its search coverage: queries run, stances found and, for any stance with no result, a recorded AbsenceFinding. A pack is never blocked for lacking contradicting evidence.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: One-sided packs built by seeking only agreement, or packs rejected because no contradiction happens to exist.

invariants.rule: Every EvidenceCandidate must carry a resolvable Provenance from EvidenceCorpus.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Unsourced evidence inside an argument.

invariants.rule: A weight breakdown (authority, relevance, recency, directness) must be present for every candidate.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Opaque single-number scoring.

invariants.rule: A frozen EvidencePack is immutable; later retrieval produces a new pack version.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Silent mutation of evidence after it justified an argument.

invariants.rule: An EvidencePack must reference the IndexManifest version and reranker model that produced it.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Irreproducible evidence after re-indexing.

invariants.rule: Authority weight must be looked up from the corpus-owned rubric, never invented by retrieval.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Two subsystems disagreeing about trust.

invariants.rule: Recency weighting applies only to perishable material; legislation, foundational studies, reference figures and institutional statutes are exempt and keep full weight regardless of age.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: A 1995 statute or foundational study outranked by a recent press mention.

invariants.rule: Balance is satisfied by truthful coverage, not fabricated doubt: an AbsenceFinding must state which queries and which corpus snapshot were searched and found nothing.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Padding a pack with tangential material to appear balanced.

boundedContexts.name: StakeholderModel
boundedContexts.description: Owns institutional identity: who the stakeholder is, what it wants, what limits it, and how that becomes a negotiating agent persona. Guarantees institutions only, never persons.
boundedContexts.subdomainRationale: Distinct, defensible institutional identity is the core of the simulation's realism.

invariants.rule: A Stakeholder is always an institution; no Stakeholder may represent or be named after a natural person.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Simulating individual politicians or officials.

invariants.rule: A StakeholderProfile must declare at least one interest and one constraint before activation.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: A positionless generic chatbot in the negotiation.

invariants.rule: Budget constraints and decision priorities must sit within the declared mandate scope.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: An agent conceding authority the institution does not have.

invariants.rule: An AgentBinding is immutable for the duration of a run.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: An agent silently changing identity mid-negotiation.

invariants.rule: NegotiatingPower must be derived from declared mandate scope, budget authority and veto rights; an agent may never assign it.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Agents inventing leverage to win an argument.

invariants.rule: A Dependency is directional and may only link two stakeholders registered in the same run.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Coalition analysis over institutions not negotiating.

invariants.rule: A VetoRight applies to a proposal class, never to a specific proposal.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Ad-hoc blocking that makes outcomes arbitrary.

invariants.rule: Every VetoRight, MandateScope and BudgetLimit must cite a MandateSource of type legislation, statutory instrument or budget decision; unsourced authority is inadmissible.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Agents inventing legal competences, veto powers or budget ceilings that no real instrument grants.

invariants.rule: A HistoricalPosition requires explicit attribution to the institution in its source; a document that merely mentions the institution does not establish a position.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Inferring a stance from a passing newspaper reference and treating it as institutional history.

invariants.rule: Where the only available attribution is weak or indirect, the HistoricalPosition must be recorded as such and cannot be used to override a current explicit statement.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Old, weakly attributed history outweighing the institution's present position.

boundedContexts.name: NegotiationSession
boundedContexts.description: The heart of the domain: a policy question becomes a mandate, stakeholders take turns, argue with evidence, revise positions, form coalitions and the run closes under an explicit stopping condition.
boundedContexts.subdomainRationale: The negotiation state machine and its invariants are the heart of the domain.

invariants.rule: A round cannot close until every bound stakeholder has taken a turn or been recorded as abstaining.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Silent skipping of a stakeholder to manufacture consensus.

invariants.rule: A position cannot be revised without a revision reason citing at least one Argument or EvidencePack id.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Arbitrary opinion flips with no explainable cause.

invariants.rule: An Argument must cite at least one EvidencePack or be explicitly marked unsupported and flagged.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Evidence-free assertions presented as justified negotiation input.

invariants.rule: Only one open Position per (stakeholder, conflict topic); revision supersedes the previous one.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Contradictory simultaneous stances by the same institution.

invariants.rule: A closed SimulationRun is immutable; further analysis yields a projection or a new run.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Post-hoc editing of a published negotiation outcome.

invariants.rule: A Coalition may only contain stakeholders and must publish one explicit shared proposal.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Vague bloc voting that hides what was actually agreed.

invariants.rule: Round count may not exceed the mandate round cap; exceeding it forces terminal evaluation.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Endless negotiation that never terminates.

invariants.rule: A turn is assigned to exactly one bound stakeholder per round; no out-of-turn or duplicate turns on the same topic.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Turn-order manipulation that lets a dominant agent drown out others.

invariants.rule: Phase transitions are monotonic; a run never returns to an earlier phase.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Looping back to erase inconvenient commitments.

invariants.rule: A Proposal component must be quantified or declared unquantified; unquantified components cannot contribute to an ImpactAssessment.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Impact figures built on measures nobody costed.

invariants.rule: Coalition membership requires an accepted CoalitionOffer; membership cannot be inferred after the fact.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Retroactive claim of support for a deal the institution never joined.

invariants.rule: Every round must persist a RoundLearning record before the next round may open.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Agents repeating the same failed argument because nothing was carried forward.

invariants.rule: A LearningApplication must cite the RoundLearning it derives from; no agent may invoke 'experience' without a persisted record.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Invented lessons that retroactively justify a position change.

invariants.rule: RoundLearning is derived from that run's own arguments and must not import outcomes from other runs.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Cross-run contamination passing as adaptation.

boundedContexts.name: ConsensusAnalysis
boundedContexts.description: Derives the negotiation result from the recorded history: consensus, majority and minority positions, unresolved conflicts, compromise packages and impact assessments. Never invents agreement.
boundedContexts.subdomainRationale: A negotiation result (not a single answer) is the required output product.

invariants.rule: ConsensusRecord, CompromisePackage and ImpactAssessment are derived artefacts: they hold no input state, and recalculation from run history must reproduce them. Only derivation metadata is authoritative.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Derived views becoming competing sources of truth that drift from the negotiation record.

invariants.rule: A ConsensusRecord may only cite stances present in the closed run's history.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Manufactured agreement.

invariants.rule: Consensus requires the mandate support threshold; below it the outcome is partial or unresolved.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Forced consensus hiding real conflict.

invariants.rule: A MinorityPosition must list its holding stakeholders and their arguments.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Dissenting institutions vanishing from the result.

invariants.rule: A CompromisePackage may only combine individually accepted, mutually compatible components.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Unimplementable bundles of contradictory measures.

invariants.rule: Every ImpactAssessment figure must declare an EstimateBasis; assumed figures must be labelled and never presented as computed.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: LLM guesses published as calculations.

invariants.rule: A figure marked measured or derived must enumerate its inputs; without inputs the basis must be assumed.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: An unbacked number labelled 'derived'.

invariants.rule: The system must never present an illustrative value from its own documentation as a run outcome.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: A demo figure such as 22% reappearing as a computed result.

invariants.rule: An ImpactAssessment must reference exactly one Scenario and one CompromisePackage.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Orphaned headline numbers the brief cannot trace.

invariants.rule: A Scenario marked feasible must name the consenting institutions required and confirm none vetoes it.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Feasibility asserted while a blocking institution opposes.

invariants.rule: Consensus may not be declared for a proposal class covered by a bound stakeholder's VetoRight.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Majority rule masquerading as consensus.

boundedContexts.name: DecisionBrief
boundedContexts.description: Projects a closed run into the publishable, jury-facing artefact with all eight required components and resolvable citations. Read-model of the negotiation, never a source of truth.
boundedContexts.subdomainRationale: The jury-facing deliverable and the artefact that proves transparency.

invariants.rule: A DecisionBrief cannot be published unless all eight required sections exist.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Incomplete artefact missing conflict or impact analysis.

invariants.rule: Every CitationReference must resolve to an existing Passage provenance at publication time.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Broken citations in the deliverable the jury inspects.

invariants.rule: A published DecisionBrief is immutable; revisions create a new version referencing the prior one.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Silent post-publication edits of an outcome.

invariants.rule: The brief must state the probabilistic nature of the simulation.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Simulated reasoning presented as deterministic fact.

invariants.rule: Every CitedStatement must carry at least one CitationReference or be explicitly marked narrative or unsupported.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Bare assertions that look evidenced but are not.

invariants.rule: A DecisionBrief must disclose every rejected proposal recorded in the run.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: A tidy result hiding refused options.

invariants.rule: The brief is a projection: it may hold no state that is not derived from the closed run, and regeneration from run history must reproduce it field for field apart from narrative wording.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: The brief becoming a second, competing source of truth about what happened.

invariants.rule: Where a run outcome is ambiguous or veto-blocked, the brief must say so; it may not smooth the result into a recommendation.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: An honest 'blocked' being rewritten as a consensus recommendation.

boundedContexts.name: SimulationOrchestration
boundedContexts.description: Agent workflow graph execution (LangGraph), progress streaming, job lifecycle, pause/resume; orchestrates but does not own state.
boundedContexts.subdomainRationale: Necessary plumbing; correctness deferred to NegotiationSession aggregates.

boundedContexts.name: ClaimValidation
boundedContexts.description: Keeps figures honest: extracts claims from arguments, verifies them against authoritative sources, detects contradictions between agents and flags unsupported assertions.
boundedContexts.subdomainRationale: Requirement that figures must not contradict each other and must be substantiated.

invariants.rule: A quantitative claim cannot be marked verified without at least one authoritative-tier source.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Press-only figures presented as verified facts.

invariants.rule: Two verified claims asserting incompatible values for the same measure and period cannot both remain verified.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Contradictory numbers circulating in one negotiation.

invariants.rule: A claim with no evidence above threshold must be marked unsupported, never silently dropped.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Unsupported assertions passing as facts.

invariants.rule: Verdicts record the source set and the comparison method used.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Opaque, unauditable verdicts.

invariants.rule: A claim is contradictable only when the difference exceeds the tolerance band of its measure.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Calling rounding a contradiction.

invariants.rule: A ReferenceFigure must name its authoritative source tier; press figures may never serve as reference values.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: The baseline drifting to whatever the newspapers printed.

invariants.rule: An escalated claim stays unverified until an ExpertReview verdict is recorded.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Ambiguity treated as settled because someone asked a question.

invariants.rule: The verification path is selected by claim type: quantitative claims compare against ReferenceFigures, legal claims against provisions, causal claims against studies, and qualitative claims are not verifiable at all.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Running a causal or qualitative claim through a number check and stamping it verified.

invariants.rule: Causal and qualitative claims may be recorded as supported, contested or unverifiable, but never as verified fact.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: A study that suggests a link being published as proven causation.

invariants.rule: Where a claim type cannot be verified by any available path, the verdict must be explicitly ambiguous rather than omitting the claim.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Unverifiable claims disappearing from the audit trail.

boundedContexts.name: GovernanceCompliance
boundedContexts.description: Rules that institutions only are represented (never real persons), no quoting of real individuals, and transparency of position derivation.
boundedContexts.subdomainRationale: Hard regulatory requirement from the challenge; enforcement must be explicit.

boundedContexts.name: IdentityAccess
boundedContexts.description: Authentication, workspace access, roles (analyst, operator, admin).

contextMap.note: Corpus publishes indexed passages with provenance; retrieval consumes as published language.
Retrieval returns EvidencePacks; negotiation maps them to ClaimEvidence refs, never raw vector hits.
Positions must reference stakeholder interests/constraints; both evolve together.
Session emits domain events consumed to derive consensus/conflict records.
Brief projects consensus records plus history into the deliverable.
Arguments with claims are gated on verification status before being accepted.
Guards agent output; rejects person-level references before persistence.
LangGraph invokes domain commands; domain state is never read from graph state.

openQuestions: RESOLVED this revision: negotiation learning (RoundLearning + LearningApplication, persisted per round, applied with an explicit citation); impact provenance (EstimateBasis: measured|derived|modelled|assumed, with enumerated DerivationInput); stakeholder authority grounding (MandateSource cites legislation/statute/budget decision; unsourced powers inadmissible); evidence balance relaxed to recorded search coverage + AbsenceFinding; claim-type verification paths (quantitative/legal/causal/qualitative, with causal and qualitative never 'verified'); authority made claim-type-relative (AuthorityRule) instead of one global scale; historical positions gated on AttributionStrength (mention is not a position); recency exemptions for non-perishable sources; quotations split by SpeakerKind so institutional statements survive while personal quotes are excluded; derived artefacts declared projections, not competing sources of truth; RetrievalQuery demoted from aggregate root; CorpusCollection and IndexManifest reduced to manifests rather than corpus-wide transactional aggregates; 8 implementation-detail events removed from the catalogue. OPEN: (1) corpus profiling — actual formats, OCR share, metadata quality, German text quality — must precede any throughput or latency target; (2) RAG ingestion contracts (segmentation of multi-clipping digests, duplicate vs syndication vs same-event clustering, BM25/dense fusion weights, reranking model, evidence classification relative to a claim) belong to the architecture pass, not this exploration; (3) database schema, index structure and embedding strategy for German; (4) API contracts and SSE event shapes; (5) worker and failure-recovery design; (6) evaluation harness for evidence quality and negotiation behaviour; (7) which stakeholder set is authoritative and who curates MandateSource citations; (8) reproducibility policy: what is replayed vs regenerated when a run is resumed. DEFERRED as post-hackathon: multi-question comparison runs, cross-run learning, multi-language UI, real-time collaboration.

functionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall ingest the full Austrian press corpus with document-level and article-level provenance (publication, date, page, source URI).
The system shall extract text from PDF/HTML/scanned documents using an OCR fallback and record an extraction quality indicator per document.
The system shall segment documents into articles and articles into citable passages with exact character offsets.
The system shall classify each source into an authority tier (press report, institutional statement, legal text, scientific study, official statistics).
The system shall detect duplicate and syndicated articles and link them to a single canonical article.
The system shall retrieve hybrid (BM25 + dense) candidate passages for a claim and rerank them before use.
The system shall assemble an EvidencePack containing supporting, contradicting and contextual evidence for a claim, never only supporting evidence.
The system shall score evidence by authority tier, relevance, recency and directness, with every score component individually inspectable.
The system shall weight recent publications more strongly than historical ones via a configurable recency policy.
The system shall maintain a registry of institutional stakeholders with mandate, interests, constraints, budget limits and decision priorities.
The system shall bind each activated stakeholder to an agent persona derived from its institutional profile and historical positions.
The system shall create a simulation run from a policy question and a negotiation mandate selecting the relevant stakeholders.
The system shall run negotiation rounds in which each stakeholder submits an evidenced initial position before debate begins.
The system shall record every argument with speaker, target, stance (support/oppose/qualify), claims and cited evidence references.
The system shall allow a stakeholder to revise its position only by recording the reason and referencing the arguments or evidence that caused the change.
The system shall record conflict topics with per-stakeholder stance and track their resolution status across rounds.
The system shall allow stakeholders to form a coalition on a conflict topic with an explicit shared proposal.
The system shall terminate a negotiation when a stopping condition fires (consensus threshold, round cap, deadlock) and record which condition fired.
The system shall derive consensus, majority and minority positions plus unresolved conflicts from the recorded negotiation history.
The system shall derive compromise packages from accepted cross-stakeholder proposal components.
The system shall present impact assessments per scenario with explicit assumptions and uncertainty labels.
The system shall generate a DecisionBrief containing all eight required components (question, actors, history, conflicts, compromises, consensus, open disputes, impact) with resolvable citations.
The system shall verify quantitative and legal claims against authoritative sources and reject arguments whose claims contradict verified figures.
The system shall flag arguments containing unsupported assertions and surface them as low-confidence in the brief.
The system shall reject any agent output that attributes positions to named real persons or quotes individuals.
The system shall disclose, for every position, how it was derived (sources, arguments, model invocation reference).
The system shall execute simulations asynchronously and stream progress events to the client.
The system shall support pausing and resuming a running simulation without losing negotiation state.
The system shall persist prompt template version, model identifier and parameters for every agent invocation.
The system shall allow reconstruction of a completed simulation's full event history and re-rendering of its brief.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall provide citation-grade provenance for every evidence reference down to article and passage.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: 100% of cited evidence resolvable to document + passage offset; 0 orphan citations in validation

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall keep domain state authoritative and independent of workflow-engine state.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: 0 domain invariants enforced inside LangGraph nodes; all state mutation via domain commands

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall stream negotiation progress to clients with low latency.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: first progress event < 2s after run start; event emitted within 1s of each domain event commit

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall retrieve and rerank evidence within an interactive budget.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: PROVISIONAL — no target until corpus profiling and a representative run. Record p50/p95 on demo hardware first, then set the budget from measurement.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall ingest the full corpus without manual per-document intervention.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: PROVISIONAL — throughput target set after profiling file types and OCR share. Requirement: ingestion is parallelisable by document and idempotent on re-run.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall protect against prompt injection and data exfiltration via retrieved documents.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: all retrieved content treated as untrusted data; zero tool invocations initiated from document text

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall enforce the institution-only representation rule at output boundaries.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: 100% of person-level or person-quoting outputs rejected pre-persistence; 0 such statements in generated briefs

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall recover from worker or agent failures without corrupting negotiation state.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: run resumable after crash; no partial argument persisted; at-least-once delivery with idempotent domain commands

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall document the reproducibility limits of probabilistic agent output.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: every run records model + prompt versions and seed; brief explicitly states non-determinism

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall bound LLM cost and latency per simulation.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: PROVISIONAL — a hard cost ceiling per run is required; the concrete number is set after one measured 9-stakeholder run.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall make every generated argument reproducible to its inputs.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: each argument stores prompt version, model, evidence pack id and round; 100% traceable

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall enforce institutional-only agent identities.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: agent identity bound to an institutional Stakeholder id; 0 agents addressable by personal name

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall isolate concurrent simulation runs.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: Isolation is mandatory (no cross-run state). Concurrency count is PROVISIONAL until measured; demo must support at least two concurrent runs.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall keep agent latency acceptable during streaming rounds.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: p95 single agent turn < 20s with streaming partial argument tokens

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall degrade gracefully when the LLM provider fails.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: bounded retries with exponential backoff; run marked paused with diagnosable failure, never partially committed argument

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall protect the security of stored simulation and corpus data.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: secrets never persisted in domain events; least-privilege DB roles; encrypted transport for all provider calls

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall keep the API contract stable for the frontend during the hackathon.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: OpenAPI schema published and versioned; contract tests green on every build

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall test domain invariants with automated coverage.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: >= 80% line coverage on domain layer; every aggregate invariant has at least one rejecting test

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall evaluate retrieval quality measurably.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: A manually labelled evaluation set of claims with known supporting and contradicting passages is required before any recall figure is set. No arbitrary recall threshold shall be specified in advance.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall keep a full audit trail of state changes.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: every aggregate transition emits a persisted domain event; history reconstructable to any round

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall bound and document ingestion failure rates.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: Every failed document is persisted with a reason and is retryable. The admissible failure rate is set after corpus profiling, not assumed.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall keep the corpus index fresh relative to ingestion.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: PROVISIONAL — a newly ingested document becomes searchable once its IndexManifest version is published; the latency bound is set after measuring index build cost.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall operate within hackathon cost constraints.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: full demo simulation (9 agents, 6 rounds) within a configured per-run token budget

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall authenticate and authorise API access.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: all mutating endpoints require an authenticated principal; role checks enforced per route; 0 unauthenticated state changes

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall expose API contracts covering all documented use cases.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: >= 95% endpoint coverage of the FR catalogue; every endpoint has request/response schema and contract test

applicationServices.useCase: Record a stakeholder's opening position with claims and cited evidence before debate opens.

applicationServices.name: TakeNegotiationTurn
applicationServices.useCase: Let a stakeholder respond within a round: submit an argument against a target position or argument, with stance and evidence.
commands: close round when all turns complete

applicationServices.name: RevisePosition
applicationServices.useCase: Change a position only with a recorded reason citing the arguments or evidence that caused the shift.

applicationServices.name: TrackConflictTopic
applicationServices.useCase: Open, update and resolve conflict topics with per-stakeholder stance across rounds.

applicationServices.name: FormCoalition
applicationServices.useCase: Join stakeholders on a conflict topic behind an explicit shared proposal.

applicationServices.name: EvaluateStoppingCondition
applicationServices.useCase: Decide whether the negotiation closes: consensus threshold, round cap or deadlock; record the fired condition.

applicationServices.name: ReplaySimulationHistory
applicationServices.useCase: Reconstruct a run to any round from persisted domain events for audit and re-render.

applicationServices.name: DeriveConsensus
applicationServices.useCase: Compute consensus, majority and minority positions and unresolved conflicts from the negotiation record.

applicationServices.name: ComposeCompromisePackage
applicationServices.useCase: Assemble accepted proposal components into a compromise package with provenance.

applicationServices.name: AssessImpact
applicationServices.useCase: Attach scenario impact estimates with assumptions and uncertainty to each package.

applicationServices.name: PublishDecisionBrief
applicationServices.useCase: Project the completed run into the eight-section brief with resolvable citations.

applicationServices.name: VerifyClaim
applicationServices.useCase: Check a quantitative or legal claim against authoritative sources and reject contradictions.

applicationServices.name: FlagUnsupportedAssertion
applicationServices.useCase: Detect claims without evidence and mark them low-confidence.

applicationServices.name: EnforceInstitutionOnlyOutput
applicationServices.useCase: Reject agent output that names or quotes real persons before it reaches persistence.

applicationServices.name: DisclosePositionProvenance
applicationServices.useCase: Produce the derivation record for each position: sources, arguments and model invocation reference.

applicationServices.name: RunSimulationJob
applicationServices.useCase: Execute the agent workflow graph as a background job, emitting progress events and supporting pause/resume.

applicationServices.name: ExtractDocumentText
applicationServices.useCase: Extract text natively when a text layer exists, fall back to OCR for scanned pages, and store the resulting extraction quality and method.

applicationServices.name: LinkCanonicalArticle
applicationServices.useCase: Detect syndicated and duplicate articles by content similarity and attach them to one canonical article so citations and evidence counts collapse correctly.

applicationServices.name: StreamSimulationProgress
applicationServices.useCase: Publish ordered progress events for a running simulation so clients observe rounds, turns and position changes as they commit.

applicationServices.name: PauseOrResumeSimulation
applicationServices.useCase: Pause a running job at a safe boundary and resume it later from persisted negotiation state without losing rounds or arguments.

applicationServices.name: RecordAgentInvocation
applicationServices.useCase: Persist the traceability envelope of every agent call: model, prompt template version, parameters, evidence pack ids and token cost.

applicationServices.name: ScoreEvidenceCandidates
applicationServices.useCase: Compute the inspectable weight breakdown for every candidate — authority weight, lexical score, semantic similarity, recency weight and directness — and rank them so the jury can see why evidence was used.

applicationServices.name: TranslateQuestionToMandate
applicationServices.useCase: Moderator-specific framing: convert the free-text policy question into a testable mandate with objective, target metric, time horizon, budget constraint and negotiation rules before any run exists.

applicationServices.name: SelectRelevantStakeholders
applicationServices.useCase: Moderator-specific selection: determine which institutions are materially affected by the mandate and may therefore be bound into the run.
commands: map mandate topics to stakeholder interests

applicationServices.name: DetectArgumentContradiction
applicationServices.useCase: Moderator-specific arbitration: detect when two stakeholders assert incompatible claims or refuse to justify a position, and force a justification turn.

applicationServices.name: SummariseIntermediateResult
applicationServices.useCase: Moderator-specific interim documentation after each round: agreed points, open conflicts, emerged options and failed proposals, so convergence is observable mid-run.

applicationServices.name: PinCorpusSnapshot
applicationServices.useCase: Freeze the exact document set and index version a run may search, so the evidence base of a published brief is reproducible after re-ingestion.

applicationServices.name: IndexIngestedPassages
applicationServices.useCase: Publish extracted passages into the hybrid index (BM25 + vectors) with provenance payloads, keeping ingestion and searchability decoupled and idempotent.

applicationServices.name: RecordGovernanceViolation
applicationServices.useCase: Persist a rejected agent output with its violation class, the offending span and the rewrite that replaced it, so the transparency rule is provably enforced.

applicationServices.name: VersionDecisionBrief
applicationServices.useCase: Republish a brief for the same run as an immutable successor version, preserving the prior version and the reason for regeneration.

applicationServices.name: CompareScenarios
applicationServices.useCase: Evaluate alternative compromise packages side by side on cost, acceptance and feasibility so the brief can state why one package was recommended over another.

applicationServices.name: RecordHistoricalPosition
applicationServices.useCase: Extract and store a provenance-backed past institutional stance from corpus evidence, weighted below current events, so personas argue from documented history rather than invention.

applicationServices.name: RecordAbstention
applicationServices.useCase: Close the gap in round-close invariant FR-014: a stakeholder that neither argues nor revises must be explicitly recorded as abstaining on a topic before the round can close.

applicationServices.name: ResolveMeasureIdentity
applicationServices.useCase: Normalise a claim's measure into a comparable identity (measure, unit, period, geography) so that figures from different agents and sources can be tested for contradiction.

domainEvents.name: DocumentIngested
domainEvents.description: A source file was registered, extracted and quality-assessed.

domainEvents.name: DocumentExtractionFailed
domainEvents.description: Extraction could not reach the acceptance threshold; document excluded from citation.

domainEvents.name: ArticleSegmented
domainEvents.description: Article boundaries and publication metadata were resolved for a document.

domainEvents.name: AuthorityTierAssigned
domainEvents.description: A source was classified into an authority tier used for evidence weighting.

domainEvents.name: DuplicateArticleLinked
domainEvents.description: A syndicated copy was linked to a canonical article so citations collapse correctly and duplicate reporting does not inflate evidence support.

domainEvents.name: EvidencePackAssembled
domainEvents.description: A balanced, scored evidence pack was frozen for a claim.

domainEvents.name: ContradictingEvidenceSurfaced
domainEvents.description: Evidence opposing the requesting stakeholder's position was found and included in the pack.

domainEvents.name: StakeholderRegistered
domainEvents.description: A new institutional stakeholder entered the registry with mandate and profile.

domainEvents.name: StakeholderProfileUpdated
domainEvents.description: Interests, constraints or priorities changed; affects all future runs but not running ones.

domainEvents.name: AgentPersonaBound
domainEvents.description: A stakeholder was bound to an agent persona for a specific run.

domainEvents.name: HistoricalPositionRecorded
domainEvents.description: A past institutional stance was extracted and stored with provenance.

domainEvents.name: MandateViolationDetected
domainEvents.description: A proposed concession exceeded the stakeholder's declared constraints or budget limits.

domainEvents.name: SimulationRunOpened
domainEvents.description: A run was created from a mandate with pinned corpus and stakeholders.

domainEvents.name: RoundOpened
domainEvents.description: A new negotiation round started with its turn order.

domainEvents.name: InitialPositionStated
domainEvents.description: A stakeholder opened its evidenced starting position.

domainEvents.name: ArgumentSubmitted
domainEvents.description: A stakeholder contributed an argument with stance, claims and citations.

domainEvents.name: PositionRevised
domainEvents.description: A stakeholder changed its position with a recorded reason and evidence.

domainEvents.name: PositionRevisionRejected
domainEvents.description: A position change was refused because no causal reason or evidence reference was supplied.

domainEvents.name: ConflictTopicOpened
domainEvents.description: Divergence between stakeholders was formalised as a tracked conflict.

domainEvents.name: CoalitionFormed
domainEvents.description: Several stakeholders aligned behind one shared proposal on a conflict topic.

domainEvents.name: RoundClosed
domainEvents.description: All turns for the round completed; convergence measured.

domainEvents.name: SimulationRunClosed
domainEvents.description: The run terminated because a stopping condition fired.

domainEvents.name: ConsensusDetermined
domainEvents.description: Consensus level for a conflict topic was derived from recorded stances.

domainEvents.name: MinorityPositionRecorded
domainEvents.description: A dissenting stance was recorded with holders and reasons.

domainEvents.name: CompromisePackageComposed
domainEvents.description: Accepted components were combined into a package with rejected proposals documented.

domainEvents.name: ImpactAssessed
domainEvents.description: Scenario impacts were estimated for a package with stated assumptions and uncertainty.

domainEvents.name: UnresolvedConflictDeclared
domainEvents.description: A conflict remained open at run close and was carried into the brief.

domainEvents.name: DecisionBriefPublished
domainEvents.description: A complete, citation-resolved brief was published for a closed run.

domainEvents.name: CitationResolutionFailed
domainEvents.description: A citation could not be resolved to a passage provenance; publication blocked.

domainEvents.name: DecisionBriefVersioned
domainEvents.description: A new brief version was produced from the same run.

domainEvents.name: ClaimExtracted
domainEvents.description: A verifiable assertion was extracted from an argument.

domainEvents.name: ClaimVerified
domainEvents.description: A claim was confirmed against an authoritative source.

domainEvents.name: ClaimRejected
domainEvents.description: A claim was contradicted by authoritative evidence; the argument may not stand on it.

domainEvents.name: UnsupportedAssertionFlagged
domainEvents.description: A claim had no adequate evidence and was flagged low-confidence.

domainEvents.name: ContradictionDetected
domainEvents.description: Two claims or a claim and an authoritative figure were found incompatible.

domainEvents.name: QuotationBlockDetected
domainEvents.description: A passage region was classified as quoted or reported speech of a person and flagged as non-promotable evidence.

domainEvents.name: DocumentQuarantined
domainEvents.description: A document failed the extraction quality gate and was excluded from the citable corpus while remaining retrievable for diagnostics.

domainEvents.name: IngestionRunCompleted
domainEvents.description: A batch ingestion finished with accepted, quarantined and failed counts recorded against the run.

domainEvents.name: IndexManifestPublished
domainEvents.description: A new index version became searchable for a corpus snapshot, making previously ingested passages citable.

domainEvents.name: PassageRevertedFromIndex
domainEvents.description: A passage was removed from the live index because its document was retracted or found unusable, so no future argument can cite it.

domainEvents.name: NegotiatingPowerChanged
domainEvents.description: An institution's derived leverage changed because its mandate scope, budget authority or veto rights changed, altering which coalitions are viable.

domainEvents.name: VetoRightRegistered
domainEvents.description: An institution's power to block a class of proposals was declared, making majority-only consensus insufficient.

domainEvents.name: DependencyRecorded
domainEvents.description: A directional dependency between two institutions was registered, enabling coalition and blockade analysis.

domainEvents.name: NegotiationPhaseAdvanced
domainEvents.description: The run entered the next process phase, changing which commands are admissible and which UI stage is shown.

domainEvents.name: CoalitionOffered
domainEvents.description: A stakeholder invited another institution to join a shared proposal with stated conditions.

domainEvents.name: CoalitionOfferDeclined
domainEvents.description: An invited institution refused a coalition on a conflict topic, with its stated reason.

domainEvents.name: ScenarioDefined
domainEvents.description: A baseline-versus-package scenario was defined with horizon, population and assumptions before any impact figure was produced.

domainEvents.name: ConsensusBlockedByVeto
domainEvents.description: A proposal reached the support threshold but cannot be recorded as consensus because an institution holds a blocking competence over its class.

domainEvents.name: FeasibilityRated
domainEvents.description: Political, legal and administrative feasibility of a package was rated with its stated basis.

domainEvents.name: RejectedProposalDisclosed
domainEvents.description: A proposal that failed to gather support was disclosed in the brief with its blockers and reasons.

domainEvents.name: BriefBlockedByMissingDisclosure
domainEvents.description: Publication was refused because a required disclosure (rejected proposal, unsupported statement or disclaimer) was absent.

domainEvents.name: ReferenceFigureRegistered
domainEvents.description: A canonical authoritative value was registered for a measure, establishing the comparison baseline for future claims.

domainEvents.name: ClaimEscalatedForReview
domainEvents.description: A claim the deterministic checks could not settle was escalated to expert review and left unverified meanwhile.

domainEvents.name: ExpertReviewResolved
domainEvents.description: An escalated claim received a verdict with its basis, settling or confirming its uncertainty.

domainEvents.name: RoundLearningCaptured
domainEvents.description: The outcome of a round was distilled into a persisted learning record consumed by every bound stakeholder in the next round.

domainEvents.name: LearningApplied
domainEvents.description: A stakeholder explicitly applied a captured insight, adapting its argument or position because of what happened earlier in this negotiation.

domainEvents.name: MandateSourceCited
domainEvents.description: An authority claim was grounded in a citable instrument, making the stakeholder's power auditable rather than asserted.

domainEvents.name: AuthorityClaimRejected
domainEvents.description: A veto right, competence or budget limit was refused because no admissible mandate source backed it.

domainEvents.name: WeakAttributionFlagged
domainEvents.description: A historical position was stored with weak or indirect attribution and marked unusable for overriding current statements.

domainEvents.name: UnbackedEstimateBlocked
domainEvents.description: An impact figure was refused because it declared a computed basis without enumerable inputs.

domainEvents.name: EvidenceAbsenceRecorded
domainEvents.description: A stance produced no qualifying evidence and the absence was recorded together with the searches that failed to find any.

domainEvents.name: PersonalQuotationExcluded
domainEvents.description: A quotation attributed to a natural person was marked non-citable so it can never reach an agent's evidence pack.

domainEvents.name: InstitutionalStatementAttributed
domainEvents.description: A statement attributed to an institution (not a person) was retained as citable evidence of that institution's position.

domainEvents.name: ClaimMarkedUnverifiable
domainEvents.description: A claim could not be verified by any applicable path and was recorded as explicitly ambiguous instead of being dropped.

domainEvents.name: CausalClaimAppraised
domainEvents.description: A causal claim was appraised against study evidence and recorded as supported, contested or unaddressed, never as verified fact.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: A physical ingested source file before editorial segmentation.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: press_archive_2020_issue_142.pdf

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: One editorial unit segmented out of a Document, carrying headline, date and page.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: 'Ärztekammer fordert mehr Kassenstellen' (2020-03-14, p. 7)

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The smallest citable text span; the unit that is indexed, retrieved and cited.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Passage #3 of Article 17, offsets 1420-1985

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Ranked credibility rubric owned by the corpus, published to consumers; retrieval never defines trust itself.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: legislation > official-statistics > scientific-study > institutional-statement > press-report

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Measured confidence that a Document's text faithfully represents the physical source.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: ocr, 0.83, 1.2% missing glyphs, accepted

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Immutable locator bundle that lets any citation be resolved to a page and offset.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: doc:D-142/article:A-17/page:7/offsets:1420-1985

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The versioned document set a simulation run searched, frozen at run start.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: corpus-2020-v3 pinned to run R-11

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Frozen, balanced and scored set of supporting, contradicting and contextual evidence for one claim.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: EvidencePack EP-88 for claim 'specialist vacancies rose 12%'

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Whether a passage supports, contradicts, contextualises or is tangential to a claim.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: contradicting

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Configured decay that weights newer publications above older ones.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: exp decay, half-life 18 months, reference 2020-12-31

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Inspectable multi-component weighting including authority, relevance, recency and directness.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: authority 1.0, bm25 8.4, cosine 0.81, recency 0.62, direct 1.0

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: State where a claim has no evidence above threshold, forcing an unsupported flag rather than an invented citation.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: gap on claim about 2035 spending projection

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Whether a passage explicitly states the claim versus merely talking about the same topic.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: direct: 'Die Wartezeiten stiegen um 22 Prozent'

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: An institution of the Austrian healthcare system represented in the negotiation. Never a natural person.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Dachverband der Sozialversicherungsträger

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Mandate, interests, constraints, budget limits and decision priorities of a Stakeholder.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: social insurance: cost containment weighted 0.4, legal competence limited to statutory benefits

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: A weighted goal the stakeholder optimises for, scoped to policy topics.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: reduce waiting times, weight 0.35

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: A hard limit the stakeholder cannot concede in negotiation.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: no additional federal spending beyond 5%

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Numeric spending envelope within which proposals are acceptable.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: +5% vs 2020 baseline by 2025

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: A provenance-backed past institutional stance, weighted lower than current events.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: 2020 statement opposing mandatory telemedicine

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Immutable link of one Stakeholder Profile to the agent that negotiates on its behalf in a run.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: run R-11 / Stakeholder SV-01 / persona v2

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: One end-to-end negotiation over one policy question.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: run R-11: waiting-time reduction question

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Moderator framing of the question: objective, constraints, actors, rules, stopping conditions.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: reduce waiting times 20% in 5 years, budget +5% max

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: A stakeholder's current evidenced stance on a conflict topic, with revision lineage.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Support telemedicine expansion for selected services

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: One turn's reasoned contribution with stance, claims and citations.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: SV: new posts create recurring cost; cites EP-88

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: A formalised point of institutional disagreement tracked across rounds.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Number of additional contract positions

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Stakeholders aligned on one conflict topic behind an explicit shared proposal.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: provinces + patient rep on rural mobile units

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Structured justification citing the arguments and evidence that caused a position change.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: moved after EP-88 contradicted cost assumption

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The named rule that terminated the run.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: round_cap_reached

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Derived per-topic outcome statement of agreement level among stakeholders.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: 4 of 9 support telemedicine expansion, threshold met

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Stance carried by most weight-bearing stakeholders on a topic.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: expansion of contract positions in shortage regions

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Dissenting stance with holders and reasons, preserved explicitly.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Ministry of Finance opposes recurring cost commitment

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Bundle of individually accepted, mutually compatible measures with provenance.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: telemedicine + contract posts + digital triage + dashboard

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: A measure that did not reach support and is documented as not carried.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: nationwide remuneration cuts

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Scenario effect estimate with explicit assumptions and uncertainty label.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: waiting time -22%, budget +4.3%, modelled, medium confidence

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Stated basis of an estimate: evidenced, modelled or assumed.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: modelled

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The complete published negotiation result artefact with eight sections and resolvable citations.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: DecisionBrief for run R-11, v1

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: One of the eight mandated components of the brief.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Conflict Analysis

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Resolvable pointer from a brief statement to an evidence passage with provenance.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: → doc D-142, p.7, offsets 1420-1985

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Institution, goals, constraints and adopted positions shown in the actors section.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Social insurance: cost containment 0.4, telemedicine supporter

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Stance trajectory per stakeholder across rounds for the change visualisation.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: patient rep: oppose → qualify → support (R1-R5)

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: A verifiable assertion from an argument, typed by what verification it requires.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: waiting times rose 22% between 2015 and 2020

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The audited verdict for a claim with its source set and comparison method.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: supported by Statistik Austria table, method: direct comparison

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: A claim with no adequate evidence, surfaced as low-confidence rather than removed.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: 'telemedicine will cut costs by half' – no evidence

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Detected incompatibility between two verified claims or a claim and an authoritative figure.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: cost figure 3.2bn vs 4.1bn for the same year

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Normalised identity of a figure (measure, unit, period, geography) enabling comparison across agents.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: waiting_time_days / AT / 2020

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: A source tier admissible for verification, as opposed to press reporting.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: SOZDOK legal text, Statistik Austria series

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Typed region of an article (headline, standfirst, body, caption, quotation) used for directness scoring and quotation screening.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: headline of A-17

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Span of quoted or reported speech of a named person; retained structurally, never promoted as agent evidence.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: '...' sagte der Obmann (excluded from evidence packs)

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The one article that owns citable passages when several syndicated copies exist.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: APA wire copy syndicated in 4 outlets → one canonical article

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: German variant marker driving tokenisation and embedding choice.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: de-AT

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: A document that failed the extraction quality gate and is excluded from citation but kept for diagnostics.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: OCR confidence 0.41 on a skewed scan

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: One auditable batch execution of corpus ingestion with accepted, quarantined and failed counts.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: run IR-7: 1,204 attempted, 1,180 accepted, 14 quarantined, 10 failed

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Published index version for a corpus snapshot, recording embedding model, indexed passages and searchable-since timestamp.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: manifest v12, model bge-m3, 480k passages, searchable since 2020-12-01T10:22Z

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: An indexed passage withdrawn because its document was retracted or reclassified as unusable.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: passage P-9912 withdrawn after rights clarification

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Numeric trust weight derived from the corpus-owned source tier; the only way retrieval may express trust.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: legislation → 1.0, press-report → 0.4

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Reproducibility record per pack: index manifest version, models used, rewrite applied, stance counts.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: manifest v12, embed bge-m3, rerank bge-reranker-v2

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Deterministic German-language expansion of a claim before search: compounds, umlauts, institutional synonyms.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: 'Kassenstellen' → 'Kassenvertragsstellen, Vertragsarztstellen'

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Derived institutional leverage from mandate scope, budget authority, veto rights and coalition centrality; never assigned by an agent.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Ministry of Finance: high budget authority, no clinical mandate

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Power to block a class of proposals outright, bounding what consensus is reachable.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: statutory benefit changes require insurer consent

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Directional relation between institutions (funding, approval, staffing, data) with strength and affected proposal classes.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: hospitals depend on provinces for investment funding

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Admissible range of agreement for an institution; bounds every concession its agent may make.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: chamber may negotiate fees, not benefit baskets

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: A stakeholder's allocated floor in a round, with order, topic and used/passed/abstained outcome.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: R3 turn 4: hospitals on financing, passed

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Monotonic process stage from position formation to closure that bounds legal commands.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: compromise

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Structured substance of a position: measure, quantified effect, target population, cost, affected institutions.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: +200 contract posts in shortage regions; EUR 84m/yr; 5-year horizon

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: One admissible part of a proposal with its own support record, assemblable into packages.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: digital specialist triage

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Recorded invitation to join a shared proposal, with conditions and accept/decline outcome.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: provinces invited patient reps to joint rural proposal; declined

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: A counterfactual assessed against a baseline: the measures of one package, a horizon, an affected population and stated assumptions.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: package P-2 vs 2020 baseline, 5-year horizon, Austria

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Political, legal and administrative feasibility of a package with the basis for each rating.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: legal: high (within insurer competence); political: medium (provinces split)

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Support level the mandate requires for consensus, adjusted where veto rights apply.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: two thirds of weight-bearing stakeholders

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: A proposal that met the support threshold but is not consensus due to a blocking competence.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: 7/9 support, blocked by insurer veto on benefit changes

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: One statement of the brief with its citations, source claim ids and evidence status; the granularity at which transparency is enforced.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: 'Waiting times fell 22% in the model' → EP-88, EP-91

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: A measure that failed to gather support, with blocking stakeholders and reasons.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: nationwide remuneration cuts — blocked by chamber + contract physicians

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Statement that the result is probabilistic agent reasoning over a pinned corpus, not a deterministic forecast and free of real-person positions.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: 'Runs are non-deterministic; model and prompt versions are recorded per run.'

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Canonical authoritative value for one measure, with as-of date and source tier; the comparison baseline.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: public_health_spend / AT / 2019 = EUR 42.1bn (Statistik Austria)

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Admissible deviation below which two figures for one measure are treated as equal.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: ±2% for survey-based measures

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Escalation of an unsettled claim to a review step that returns a verdict with its basis.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: claimed 12% rise; two surveys disagree; escalated

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Persisted digest of a round's outcomes — which arguments held, which proposals moved, who coalesced — that agents must consume in the next round.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: R2 learning: insurer's cost estimate was contradicted by EP-88

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Explicit reference from a later argument to the RoundLearning insight that caused it.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: medical chamber drops post-count demand citing R2 learning

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Citable legal or institutional instrument that grounds a veto right, competence or budget limit.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: ASVG provision on benefit changes requiring insurer consent

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Whether a source explicitly attributes a stance to the institution, reports it, or merely mentions the institution.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: explicit attributed statement vs passing mention

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Where an institution's authority derives from: legislation, statutory instrument, budget decision, institutional statute or agreement.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: budget decision

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Provenance class of a figure: measured, derived, modelled, assumed or not estimated.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: derived from two ReferenceFigures

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Enumerated input behind a derived figure, cited so the calculation can be re-run or refuted.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: RF-14 public_health_spend/AT/2019 + RF-22 population 2020

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: A figure without enumerated inputs, publishable only with an explicit assumed label.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: budget impact assumed at +4% pending costing

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Auditable record that a stance produced no qualifying evidence, naming the queries and snapshot searched.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: no contradicting evidence for a telemedicine cost claim; 6 queries over snapshot v12

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Designation of non-perishable source types (legislation, foundational studies, reference figures) that keep full weight regardless of age.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: statutory provision from 1955 exempt

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Attribution class of a statement: institution, named person, anonymous or unattributed; decides citability.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: institution: Dachverband der Sozialversicherungsträger

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Claim-type-specific source ordering used instead of one global authority scale.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: quantitative: statistics > study > institutional statement > press

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Retained, citable statement attributed to an institution rather than a person.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: chamber statement on contract posts, citable with attribution

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Type-specific route a claim takes: reference comparison, provision check, study appraisal, or no verification.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: causal → study appraisal

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Appraisal of study evidence behind a causal claim, recorded as supported, contested or unaddressed.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: observational study, contested effect direction

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: A claim for which no applicable verification path exists, recorded as ambiguous rather than removed.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: 'patients feel more secure' — qualitative, unverifiable
